messages:
Kai: Heads-up — ApexHealth asking for a pricing exception on their 12mo Dedicated commit. They want 40% off list for a $600k/yr commit (~$50k/mo) plus 3 months free. Procurement says competitor pricing is aggressive and they need netting to budget. Can we get a quick sanity check?

Elaine: 40% is pretty aggressive. What discount tier do we normally apply at $600k? Last comparable was ~25% for HealthCo at $350k.

Marco: SR tier refresh: 12mo $600k typically sits in the 20–25% band. We can push to 30% with CS reference + strict SOW. Anything >30% triggers Deal Desk + CRO signoff.

Sofia: Also worth noting — their security and legal team are asking for SOC2 + HIPAA addendum. That adds implementation/ops risk which should factor into pricing.

Kai: Timeline is tight — procurement wants a signed order by EOM. PoC on Dedicated is positive. They argue 40% because they’re moving a large incumbant and want preferred-vendor pricing.

Annie-L (Legal): HIPAA BAA doable but need to classify data flows first. If we add HIPAA commitments we should escalate to Security for scoping; that may affect T&Cs and delivery timeline.

Marco: Quick math: 40% + 3mo free => first-year blended discount ~42.5%. That pushes gross margin under our threshold for this cohort. Options: reduce free months to 1, require partial upfront, or offer 35% now with a year-2 uplift.

Kai: What's the fastest operational path? Customer will pull if we stall.

Marco: Recommendation: 1) Approve up to 30% immediately (no exec signoff). 2) Offer conditional 35% if ApexHealth provides measurable PoV metrics, a CS reference, and commits to a case study. 3) Reserve 40% only with CRO + CS leadership approval plus either upfront payment or a 24mo term.

Sofia: For the HIPAA piece, tagging security for a quick scope. If security needs changes, that could justify a smaller concession.

DealDeskBot: New deal submission created: DD-2026-1423. Status: pending review. Link: https://redwood/deals/DD-2026-1423

Kai: I'll propose the conditional 35% and push for a 6mo prepay to protect us. Marco — can you run a quick blended TCO comparing 30% / 35% / 40% scenarios (ARR, gross margin, payback) and drop it here by EOD? Need numbers for procurement.

Marco: On it — sending preliminary calc now.

Marco: ```
Prelim numbers (annualized):
- List ARR: $600,000
- 30% net -> ARR $420,000; est gross margin ~44%
- 35% net -> ARR $390,000; est gross margin ~39%
- 40% net -> ARR $360,000; est gross margin ~33%
Notes: 3mo free reduces first-year ARR further. Upfront 6mo prepay improves cash/payback materially.
```

Elaine: If CS can commit to a customer reference + joint PR, that's probably worth another ~3–5% concession.

Annie-L (Legal): If we move forward and include the BAA/HIPAA language we should not loosen indemnity/cap language for deals with >30% discount.

Kai: Copy. Tagging @Maya (CRO) for 40% exception review. Maya — please advise when you’re free.

Maya (CRO): In meetings until 16:00 PT. Initial position: 40% is only acceptable with (a) 24mo term OR (b) 12mo + 6mo upfront + executive sponsorship + reference. Otherwise push for 35% with conditions. Ping me after Marco posts final calc.

Marco: Uploaded spreadsheet (internal link). Will DM stakeholders the sensitivity tables.

DealDeskBot: Reminder — docs missing for submission: procurement PO template, SOW, and completed security questionnaire.

Kai: I'll gather the PO and SOW and ask procurement to fast-track. Thanks all :thumbsup:
